own_questions: Does the core boundary preserve the fixed scenario's four acceptance behaviors (durable personal accumulation, URL-anchored records that open the external page, create/move classifications with persistence, and browse-or-search retrieval) without importing upstream feature breadth?
Can one owner save a link with only its URL, see it land in the default inbox or a chosen collection, and later reopen the live page in a new tab while the library stays in place?
Can the owner create a collection, file a record into it, refile it repeatedly including back to the inbox, and see assignments and counts persist after reopening?
Are browsing, search, and ordering restricted to the owner's own records within one active collection, with exactly one owner role and no shared, public, or permission-denied surface?
Are the inbox, bookmark, library, and collection states mutually consistent across save, edit, move, and rename, including records that are always in exactly one collection?
Is every upstream observation an exact quote from the pinned file and range, free of runtime claims, while the partial five-file snapshot and unresolved product questions remain explicit?

Does every action and rule have a declarative given/when/then/negative assertion, and do all four scope slices carry the dependency closure and independent assertions without deferring anything a selected journey actually needs?
Are limits left open rather than inventing length or count ceilings, and does the r4 patch fix every parent diagnostic while leaving confirmed capabilities and source bindings intact?
